Distribution, Habitat, and Phenology — This species is known from the central Chocó and eastern Valle del Cauca departments of Colombia, west of the Andes (Fig. 6). They are vines or slender lianas of tropical pluvial forest, growing in primary or disturbed primary forest, on shrubby vegetation, or along creeks from 10 – 100 m elevation. Flowering specimens were collected in January, February, May, and July; the single collection seen with fruit was collected in February. Field notes describe their flowers as green or brownish.
